subject: ZenWave short-run booster: timebox add-on vs capacity slab

Subject: ZenWave short-run booster: timebox add-on vs capacity slab

Hi Arielle —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I put together two pragmatic paths to keep your 30-day POC running at full speed if you need a short runway:

1) Burst add-on (10-day): a fixed add-on that gives you guaranteed burst capacity (higher concurrency) for 10 days. Ideal if you expect a short, intense test (spike-based).
2) Capacity slab (graduated top-up): add a small committed slab for 30 days priced at a blended per-token rate that falls as usage increases. Better if you want predictable throughput across the remainder of the POC.

Key tradeoffs:
- Burst add-on is quick to approve and cheaper for short spikes but billable as a flat add-on.
- Capacity slab smooths unit cost if you plan steady high throughput and preserves cache locality (lower latency).

I've attached a quick quote contrasting the two (zenwave_burst_quote_v1.pdf) and a draft terms addendum that maps to each option (pocextension_terms_draft.docx).

Ask: could you share which pattern matches your next two weeks of testing? If you want, we can also add a 48-hour emergency surge clause (no extra legal review) to either path.

If it's helpful, I can loop in Marissa (pricing) and Karthik (solutions) to run numbers with your expected daily token burn.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Ben —

Appreciate the clear options. Quick answers from our side:

- We expect a 3–5x spike in inference calls over the next 7–10 days while we run a synthetic load against our agent demo. Latency is the bigger issue than pure tokens.
- Legal prefers a single amendable add-on rather than a month-long commitment; they want to avoid prorated invoices if we end early.

Questions:
- For the burst add-on, can you confirm whether the burst is enforced by priority routing (i.e., guaranteed slot reservation) or by soft-queueing? We need true reserved concurrency for the demo.
- If we pick the burst add-on, can Redwood convert any unused portion of the add-on into credits toward a future month? Legal asked about crediting but wants the option to decline.

If the burst can guarantee concurrency and we can get a partial-credit escape, we will take the 10-day burst. Otherwise we may prefer a smaller capacity slab.

CCing contracts@zenwave.ai for visibility.

Thanks —
Arielle Park
Director, Product Integrations | ZenWave

ZenWave prefers a 10-day burst if we can guarantee reserved concurrency and offer a partial-credit escape in case they underutilize. They explicitly want:

- True reserved concurrency for the burst window (no soft-queueing).
- Option to convert unused days to token credits at a discounted rate (not full cash refund). Legal wants the conversion to be optional on ZenWave's side.

My proposed commercial terms to test internally:
- 10-day burst add-on priced at $12,000 flat (includes reservation of N GPU slots adequate for their projected 3–5x spike).
- Unused portion conversion: ZenWave may elect within 7 days post-burst to convert up to 50% of unused days into credits at 70% of the add-on daily value. Credits expire 6 months from issuance.
- Operational SLA during burst: 99.5% availability for the reserved concurrency; credits for missed availability measured per-day.

Karthik — tech confirm: can our routing guarantee reserved slots for a 10-day window and still autoscale other customers? If yes, are there any additional ops fees we should bake into the quote?

Marissa — pricing sanity check: is $12k aggressive for 10 days of true reservation? If operations needs a premium, we can split the difference and propose $14k with a 50% refundable credit clause.

Goal: send a clean option to Arielle by EOD Wednesday.

Ben
